## Quick start A few options to get `llama.cpp` installed on your machine: ```bash # curl curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh # powershell irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex ``` - Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions - Run with Docker - see our [Docker documentation](docs/docker.md) - Download pre-built binaries from the [releases page](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases) - Build from source by cloning this repository - check out [our build guide](docs/build.md) Once installed: ```sh # Download and run a model directly from Hugging Face llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF # Launch OpenAI-compatible API server llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF ```
VLM session with llama cli Built-in web UI against llama serve
## Description The main goal of `llama.cpp` is to enable LLM (and VLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud. - Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies - Apple silicon is a first-class citizen - optimized via ARM NEON, Accelerate and Metal frameworks - AVX, AVX2, AVX512 and AMX support for x86 architectures - RVV, ZVFH, ZFH, ZICBOP and ZIHINTPAUSE support for RISC-V architectures - 1.5-bit, 2-bit, 3-bit, 4-bit, 5-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit integer quantization for faster inference and reduced memory use - Custom CUDA kernels for running LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs (support for AMD GPUs via HIP and Moore Threads GPUs via MUSA) - Vulkan and SYCL backend support - CPU+GPU hybrid inference to partially accelerate models larger than the total VRAM capacity The `llama.cpp` project is build on top of the [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml) library. ## Supported backends | Backend | Target devices | | --- | --- | | [BLAS](docs/build.md#blas-build) | All | | [BLIS](docs/backend/BLIS.md) | All | | [CANN](docs/build.md#cann) | Huawei Ascend NPU | | [CUDA](docs/build.md#cuda) | Nvidia GPU | | [HIP](docs/build.md#hip) | AMD GPU | | [Hexagon](docs/backend/snapdragon/README.md) | Snapdragon | | [IBM zDNN](docs/backend/zDNN.md) | IBM Z & LinuxONE | | [MUSA](docs/build.md#musa) | Moore Threads GPU | | [Metal](docs/build.md#metal-build) | Apple Silicon | | [OpenCL](docs/backend/OPENCL.md) | Adreno GPU | | [OpenVINO [In Progress]](docs/backend/OPENVINO.md) | Intel CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs | | [RPC](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/rpc) | All | | [SYCL](docs/backend/SYCL.md) | Intel GPU | | [VirtGPU](docs/backend/VirtGPU.md) | VirtGPU APIR | | [Vulkan](docs/build.md#vulkan) | GPU | | [WebGPU](docs/build.md#webgpu) | All | | [ZenDNN](docs/build.md#zendnn) | AMD CPU | ## Documentation #### Tools - releases.name: b12061
releases.body:
<details open>

mtmd: Pocket tts - support for voices without voice cloning (#31429)

* feat: support PocketTTS voices with no voice cloning

The kyutai/pocket-tts-without-voice-cloning weights ship predefined voices as the
backbone KV state after the voice prompt. The converter turns each state back into
the prompt embeddings and stores them in the mmproj (voice.<name>), the zeroed voice
encoder is left out, and the "voice" field of /tts and --tts-voice select one of them.
A speaker reference is rejected when the model has no voice encoder.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1

* convert : pocket-tts voices never fail the conversion, log the drift of the state

The voice states shipped by Kyutai are not always the ones the pack's
weights give for the prompt: italian, german and spanish match within the
bf16 rounding, english_2026-04 is 2% off and french 20% (its layer 0 state
comes from other weights), while the reference loads them as is and they
still sound like the same voice. The converter now re-prompts the backbone
with the recovered embeddings, compares the whole state and logs the
distance per voice, warning above 5%. A state that does not belong to the
weights at all is skipped

releases.name: b12059
releases.body:
<details open>

llama : flash_attn_ext_rows - more efficient unified kv for multi-seq (#29510)

* llama : use llm_attn_mask and kv_rows for unified attention

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov <ggerganov@gmail.com>

* cont : optimize `get_seq_cells`

* llama : build the kv_rows lists from per-sequence cell bitmaps

Keep a bitmap over the cells for each sequence (the transpose of `seq`), updated in seq_pos_inc/dec, and build the cell lists by walking its set bits. The lists stay in cell order, cells shared by several sequences go to every list, and nothing has to be rebuilt when cells are removed.

Also leave out of the lists the cells that the SWA hides from every token of the slice (standard and chunked SWA).

* cont : make get_kv_rows_p_min private

* cont : minor metal

* llama : use kv_rows for every ubatch of a unified cache

A ubatch made of equal-length runs with a single sequence each (f.ex. the drafts of several slots) now splits into per-sequence slices.

llama.cpp

LLM inference in C/C++

ggml / ops / maintainer PRs / dev stats / lib llama API / llama-server REST API

Quick start

A few options to get llama.cpp installed on your machine:

# curl
curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh

# powershell
irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
  • Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions
  • Run with Docker - see our Docker documentation
  • Download pre-built binaries from the releases page
  • Build from source by cloning this repository - check out our build guide

Once installed:

# Download and run a model directly from Hugging Face
llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF

# Launch OpenAI-compatible API server
llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF
VLM session with llama cli Built-in web UI against llama serve

Description

The main goal of llama.cpp is to enable LLM (and VLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud.

  • Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies
  • Apple silicon is a first-class citizen - optimized via ARM NEON, Accelerate and Metal frameworks
  • AVX, AVX2, AVX512 and AMX support for x86 architectures
  • RVV, ZVFH, ZFH, ZICBOP and ZIHINTPAUSE support for RISC-V architectures
  • 1.5-bit, 2-bit, 3-bit, 4-bit, 5-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit integer quantization for faster inference and reduced memory use
  • Custom CUDA kernels for running LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs (support for AMD GPUs via HIP and Moore Threads GPUs via MUSA)
  • Vulkan and SYCL backend support
  • CPU+GPU hybrid inference to partially accelerate models larger than the total VRAM capacity

The llama.cpp project is build on top of the ggml library.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A highly optimized C/C++ inference engine for running large language models locally on consumer hardware.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a standalone implementation for evaluating large language models directly on standard consumer hardware. It achieves remarkable performance by eschewing heavy Python dependencies in favor of pure C and C++ execution. The engine supports diverse hardware backends, dynamically allocating tensor operations across available CPUs and GPUs to maximize throughput. It implements advanced quantization techniques, drastically reducing memory requirements without significantly compromising model accuracy. Developers can integrate the engine into diverse applications using its extensive bindings and the bundled HTTP server.
keyFeatures: Hardware acceleration: Supports execution across Apple Silicon, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and standard x86 CPUs.
Model quantization: Implements integer quantization formats from 1.5-bit to 8-bit to reduce VRAM consumption dramatically.
Zero dependencies: Compiles as a single standalone executable without requiring external Python environments or heavy frameworks.
Continuous batching: Processes multiple concurrent inference requests efficiently through the bundled OpenAI-compatible server.
Extensive bindings: Provides wrappers for numerous programming languages including Python, Go, Rust, and Node.js.

useCases.description: Deploy highly optimized conversational agents directly onto resource-constrained edge devices and mobile phones.
